Her mother, the formidable Duchess of Kent, reportedly spent years preparing Victoria for rule, aware that life—or disease—could elevate a relatively obscure child to global power. Victoria’s accession at age 18 was sudden and almost unprepared, yet she stepped into one of the most influential positions in Europe with startling composure. The fact that a single twist of mortality changed British history underscores how fragile hereditary succession truly was. It’s a reminder that empires, despite their grandeur, can hinge on seemingly mundane events.
